A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 54-page versions of the same HoT paper. The main text, figures, tables, equations, references and Appendices A–W support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v5 reports original benchmark evaluations, ablations, fine-tuning experiments and a 63-participant human verification study (Section 5), with additional empirical analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: v6 retains these original benchmark, fine-tuning and human-study results, together with the appendix experiments and analyses.

M1.justification: The XML-linked question-and-answer procedure, three-step demonstration construction (Section 3), fine-tuning approach and appendix variants are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both retain the same reasoning, long-context, ReasoningTrap and OOD benchmarks, plus human verification on GSM-Symbolic and DROP. No datasets or test scenarios are added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain CoT, RQ, CoT + Self-Consistency and ComplexCoT (Table 10), and LtM, CoVE, Self-Refine and ToT (Table 11). The base and CoT-finetuned controls in Table 13 also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The 8-shot evaluations, model configurations, sample sizes, hallucination-judging procedures and human-study design are unchanged, including Appendix A's response filtering and time-limit handling.

E4.justification: Component and tag-format ablations, mismatched-tag tests, attention analyses, failure cases and Appendix W's over-trust mitigation analysis are retained without revisions.

E5.justification: Run-count disclosures and uncertainty reporting are identical, including five-run evaluations and standard deviations in Tables 10–11. No statistical estimation procedures are added or revised.

E6.justification: Numerical results, rankings and qualitative examples match throughout. In both PDFs, Table 1 reports averages of 21.22 for CoT and 14.92 for HoT; Table 12 reports verification times of 62.38 and 47.26 seconds, respectively. Appendix results also match.

T1.justification: The overhead and verification-accuracy formulas in Appendices C–D, attention definitions and Equations 1–2 in Appendix E, and attention-entropy expression in Table 14 are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about hallucination reduction, reasoning accuracy, faster human verification and fine-tuning benefits, including the warning that highlights can increase trust in incorrect answers.

C2.justification: Interpretations and limitations remain unchanged, including attention redistribution, small-model formatting failures, token overhead, task-specific demonstrations and over-trust concerns (Sections 5–8 and associated appendices).

D1.justification: Model/API settings, prompts, processing instructions and embedded code-access links are unchanged. The new acknowledgment credits funding and API support without adding experimental or reproducibility instructions.

R1.justification: Related-work discussion, cited works and the reference list are unchanged. The added publication and OpenReview information does not revise research positioning or novelty claims.

P1.justification: v6 adds Trung Bui's email, an OpenReview notice and a short Acknowledgments section after Section 8, and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. Scientific prose and narrative organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v6 adds a TMLR publication header throughout and modestly reflows the opening pages around retained figures and tables. Every appendix page is visually identical below the new header; no scientific displays are added or removed.

improvement.justification: v6 adds publication/contact information and funding attribution, with limited layout reflow. The scientific argument, empirical evidence, reproducibility documentation and limitations remain unchanged across the main text and appendices. These administrative additions do not materially improve or impair overall paper quality.
